also: if my memory serves me right

terms.grammar: verb: perfect in form with present sense; imperative mementō, mementōte
terms.comment: What one remembers in the genitive or accusative, or as a clause; with a present infinitive for a scene one saw (meminī Catōnem mēcum disserere, Cic. Lael. 11, Lewis & Short). Mementō with an infinitive is “remember to …, be sure to …”; sī bene meminī, if I remember rightly (Traupman 106).

evidence: Verg. A. 3.107: sī rīte audīta recordor

terms.grammar: phrase: ablative of memoria with teneō
evidence: Cic. Sen. 12; Caes. BG 1.14 (Lewis & Short, s.v. memoria)

terms.gloss: go over in one’s mind; more often, mention
evidence: Cic. Sen. 38: quid quōque diē dīxerim, audierim, ēgerim, commemorō vesperī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Traupman gives it first for “remember”, but in Lewis & Short its usual sense is “recount, mention”, and “call to mind” is rare.

terms.gloss: as I recall, as far as I remember
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.31.4: ut mea memoria est (Lewis & Short s.v. memoria)
Traupman 106: as I recall, ut mea memoria est

terms.gloss: as a reminder, to help the memory
evidence: Cic. Phil. 1.19: sī quid memoriae causā rettulit in libellum (Lewis & Short s.v. libellus)
Traupman 106: as a reminder, memoriae causā

phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

phrases.latin: aequam mementō rēbus in arduīs servāre mentem
phrases.english: remember to keep a level head when things are hard

phrases.latin: sī meminī, fuerant tibi quattuor, Aelia, dentēs
phrases.english: if I remember rightly, Aelia, you had four teeth
they remember everything they care about
If my memory serves me right …
